Methods of data transmission
How bits get from one device to another
 Leyth · Aarush
The big picture
Every transmission answers two questions
01
How many bits travel at once?
Serial
Parallel
02
Which direction does data flow?
Simplex
Half-duplex
Full-duplex
Answer both, and you’ve described any connection between two devices.
Question 1 · How many bits at once?
Serial transmission
Bits travel one after another, down a single wire.
Advantages
  • Bits always arrive in order: no skew
  • Reliable over long distances
  • Cheaper, because it needs fewer wires
Drawbacks
  • Slower than parallel over short distances
  • Only one bit can be sent at a time
Question 1 · How many bits at once?
Parallel transmission
Several bits travel at the same time, each down its own wire.
Advantages
  • Faster over short distances
  • A whole byte can arrive in one go
Drawbacks
  • Skew and interference (crosstalk)
  • More expensive, short distances only
The catch with parallel
Skew: bits arrive out of sync
0 / 1 = arrived in time · ? = late bit, so the data is wrong
The wires are never exactly the same, so some bits arrive late.
Think of a motorway
8 lanes, 8 cars. Some hit traffic. The receiver reads every lane at the same moment, so late cars mean wrong data.
Longer cable → worse skew. That’s why parallel is short-distance only.

Rule of thumb
Question 2 · Which direction?
Simplex, half-duplex, full-duplex
Simplex
One direction only. e.g. TV broadcast, computer → printer
Half-duplex
Both directions, but not at the same time. e.g. walkie-talkie
Full-duplex
Both directions at the same time. e.g. phone call, broadband
Putting it together
The two choices combine
Every real connection picks one answer to each question.
Network cable
Sends and receives at the same time
Serial
Full-duplex
USB 2.0 cable
Talks both ways, but takes turns
Serial
Half-duplex
Internal data bus
Moves data between the CPU and memory
Parallel
Half-duplex
Old printer cable
Computer sends, printer only listens
Parallel
Simplex

Quick check
A walkie-talkie sends one bit at a time, and only one person can talk at once. Which method is it?
Serial
Half-duplex
One bit at a time → serial. Takes turns → half-duplex.
Recap
What to remember
How many bits?
Serial: 1 bit at a time. Long distance, reliable, cheap.
Parallel: many bits at once. Fast, but skew keeps it short-distance.
Which direction?
Simplex: one way only.
Half-duplex: both ways, taking turns.
Full-duplex: both ways at once.
